protocol.description:
Lets a client tint everything the compositor shows with a warm color, the way a "night light" does, to be easier on the eyes in the evening. The compositor only applies the filter; *when* it should be on (a schedule, a manual toggle) is entirely the client's business, so the shell can own that policy without the compositor knowing about clocks or settings.
The filter is tied to the lifetime of the object: when a client destroys it or disconnects (including by crashing), the filter it requested is removed, so a dead shell can never leave the screen tinted. If several live objects have requested a filter, the most recent set_color_temperature request wins. Binding the global or creating an object requests nothing by itself. When the object that made the most recent request goes away, the most recent request of the remaining live objects takes over (or no filter, if there are none).
The filter always applies to every output; there is no per-output control in this version.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Removes whatever filter this object requested.

request.name: set_color_temperature

description.summary: warm the display to a color temperature

request.description:
Tints every output toward `kelvin`, a correlated color temperature in the usual night-light sense: 6500 is neutral (no tint), and lower values are progressively warmer/more orange. Values above 6500 are treated as 6500 (neutral) and values below 1000 as 1000. Passing 0 is a convenience for "no filter" and is equivalent to 6500.
Takes effect on the next frame. The change applies to every output, including ones connected later. The compositor may implement it as a true per-channel color scaling (e.g. a display gamma ramp) or as an approximating overlay, so it need not appear in screenshots.
